goal: Mirror the current linked Google Form response sheet into PostgreSQL and keep its recorded response count synchronized without inventing rows or rewriting Form Copilot job history.
target: Form Copilot backend, PostgreSQL response mirror, production API and the linked owner-controlled Google response sheet.
includes: Read the linked sheet CSV source and validate its fixed 53-column response contract
Atomically upsert the complete response mirror and record source count, digest, freshness and sync errors
Expose read-only reconciliation status while preserving existing fixed_batches and fixed_jobs audit history
Deploy the verified migration and worker to the existing production VPS
Verify that PostgreSQL mirrored response count equals the live Google Responses count without submitting a new response
excludes: Changing Google Form answers, deleting responses or changing Sheet sharing
Reclassifying uncertain jobs without row-level evidence
Sending any new Google Form response
Publishing raw response contents through the public API or frontend
outputs: PostgreSQL response mirror and sync-state migration
Periodic backend synchronization and read-only reconciliation metadata
Parser, atomic replacement and failure-regression tests

doneWhen.evidence: The backend validates and atomically mirrors every linked-sheet response while preserving job history and failing closed on malformed input.
The additive production migration is applied once without deleting or rewriting existing batch and job history.
Typecheck, tests and production build pass for the response synchronization change.
The verified image is deployed healthy to the declared Form Copilot production domains.
A read-only production check proves the PostgreSQL mirror count equals the live owner-visible Google Responses count with no new submission.

verification: Exercise valid and malformed CSV fixtures locally, verify transaction rollback and history preservation, deploy once, then compare production reconciliation metadata with the owner-visible Google Responses total.
example: When Google Forms shows 216 responses, the latest successful sync reports 216 mirrored rows with the same source digest and leaves fixed_jobs unchanged.

impacts.behavior: A validated response-sheet snapshot replaces the PostgreSQL mirror atomically while fixed job and batch audit history remains independent and unchanged.
evidence: Production read-only count parity against the owner-visible response total

business.reason: The response mirror has an explicit non-authoritative relation to job history.
verification: No job-history rewrite and no fabricated response

architecture.reason: CSV ingestion, transaction ownership and failure retention cross external and database boundaries.
verification: Malformed input cannot replace last good mirror

backend.reason: The API service needs a parser, scheduler and repository operations.

data.reason: Additive response and sync-state tables are required.
verification: Existing fixed_batches and fixed_jobs remain unchanged

api.reason: Operators need safe reconciliation metadata without raw answers.

interface.reason: No frontend or response-content UI is authorized in this mission.

audit.reason: No rendered interface changes are included.

uat.reason: Production parity must be observed against the browser-owned response count.
verification: Counts match without a new submission

quality.reason: Deployment requires one frozen technical gate.

reconciliation.reason: Delivered behavior must reconcile to the no-fabrication business boundary.
verification: Every promise maps to source and evidence
